domain.value: An assurance system for products an agent helped build: it drives real Chrome, measures what the page painted against what somebody signed, and returns a verdict with the evidence behind it. It is not a linter and not a test runner — nothing here concludes anything about a claim nobody has put their name to.

value.does: signs a promise, grants a waiver with an expiry, decides what is worth measuring at all
value.cannot: hand the signing to the machine
value.pain: what was decided dies at handover, and no instrument says how far it has drifted since
value.arrives: days or weeks after the decision, asking whether it still holds

value.who: the agent that writes the interface
value.does: drafts proposals, runs the measurement, fixes what a citation points at
value.pain: reporting done while holding broken evidence in its hand
value.arrives: straight from a terminal, seconds after a run it already saw

value.who: the developer at the pull request
value.does: blocks a merge, reads drift down to the element and the file
value.cannot: turn a finding into a blocking gate on their own
value.pain: an instrument that is wrong three times is switched off for good
value.arrives: from a diff, asking what this change moved

value: Signing is the one act the machine may not perform for itself; everything else it may propose and run.
Evidence stays in the project that produced it — the index in ~/.uxcli holds pointers, never proof.
A rule whose method is unproven may report a finding and may never report a fail.
Nothing unsigned returns fail; it returns not-committed.
